Replacement search — the field, swept three ways

🚐

The one I’m actually getting — a 2012 Mazda5. But what is it?

Short answer: it’s a compact MPV — a “mini-minivan.” It drives and parks like a regular car (about the size of a Mazda3 hatchback), but it has two sliding rear doors like a minivan and three rows of seats inside. Not a truck, not an SUV, not a big full-size van — it’s the practical in-between: minivan usefulness shrunk down to car size.

The honest version: 1 owner, ~129K miles, clean title, and it drove great — a cheap, practical interim van to get me rolling again. Two people + the dogs fit easy, and the 3rd row folds flat when I need cargo space instead of seats.

Cars.com + every franchise's own site + 8 town clusters · fully swept 2026-08-30 · target = a comfy daily for 2 people + 2 dogs ($5–13K), cushion first. The shortlist up top is the narrowed field — go drive it. Rows flagged ⚠ reason are known-problem platforms; the mid seller badge means buyer-beware, not skip — a clean car can hide there.
Seller tier: rep reputable — franchise / vetted independent, court-safe paper trail mid mid-low — independent/BHPH, go cash-ready + PPI, gem possible flag known bad actor (curbstoner/fraud) — shown, red

ModelYearsEngineTransmissionWhat to watch
Grand Caravan / Town & Country2011–2020 3.6 Pentastar V6 (port ✓)62TE 6-spd 62TE is the money risk — shudder / slip / limp (locked in 2nd–3rd). Root cause = old ATF+4. Also oil-cooler-housing leak + TIPM fuel-pump relay. Stow’n Go = best dog layout.
Grand Caravan / T&C2008–2010 3.3 / 3.8 / 4.0 V6 (port)4-spd → 62TE (’10) Older, simpler, pre-Pentastar. Fewer surprises but tired by now; still drive-test the trans.
Journey (V6)2011+ 3.6 Pentastar V6 (port ✓)62TE 6-spd Good engine, same 62TE risk as the vans. IIHS small-overlap “Poor.”
Journey (4-cyl)2011+ 2.4 World Gas (port ✓)41TE 4-spd Engine OK (RepairPal 4/5) but watch overheating ~78K (thermostat/coolant-port debris). The 4-speed is ALSO weak (slips / rough with age) — it dodges the 62TE, not transmission risk. Slow & thirsty; eats rear brakes; IIHS “Poor.” Cheapest lane.
Journey (early V6)2009–2010 ⚠ 2.7 V6 (weak)— Avoid — the weak 2.7; treat as a hard no.
Durango2011+ 3.6 Pentastar V6 ✓ / ⚠ 5.7 Hemi8-spd (later) Get the V6, not the Hemi (thirsty + MDS lifters). TIPM electrical. AWD available — the one that adds winter capability.
The engines are mostly fine — the TRANSMISSION is the gate on every Dodge. V6 = the 62TE (shudder/slip/limp); 2.4 Journey = the weak 41TE 4-speed. Either way: cold-start + warm drive through every gear + ELM327 scan. That one test decides any Dodge on this board. And any 2011–2013 Pentastar also needs a cold-start listen for the head/valve-seat tick (fixed ’14+).

$/1k left = price ÷ (250,000 − odometer) ÷ 1,000 — what each remaining thousand miles costs, assuming these platforms reach 250K. Crude on purpose: it flatters cheap, worn-out cars. Use it to break ties between similar vehicles, not as a ranking.

Region, not raw mileage. Straight-line distance lies across a state border: Palmyra NJ is 15 mi and one bridge, while South Amboy is 62 mi up the Turnpike toward NYC metro. Those are not the same trip scaled differently, so Turnpike, NY metro and MD rows are pinned to the slowest bucket regardless of mileage and are hidden at the default setting. Delaware rows are Wilmington/Newark, roughly the same drive as Reading. Every car here needs a pre-purchase inspection before money moves.
